reason: The hypothesis directly restates the mechanism and findings of P3 and P15, which already report that lattice distortion in a NiCoCrAl MPEA elevates vacancy formation energy and Al migration barriers, suppressing Al diffusion and leading to a thinner, more adherent Al2O3 scale with lower oxidation kinetics. The proposed intervention (severe plastic deformation to create an ultrafine-grained microstructure) and the predicted outcome (lower kp, thinner Al2O3) are already demonstrated in P13 and P6/P22 for similar alloy systems. The hypothesis does not combine findings from different papers into a new proposal, transfer an idea to a new alloy with a stated reason, or propose a test that resolves a conflict or gap; it merely proposes to repeat a known result with a different processing method.
copied_elements: lattice distortion suppresses Al diffusion by raising vacancy formation energy and migration barrier
lower parabolic rate constants and thinner Al2O3 scales in processed samples
comparison of as-cast vs. severely deformed samples
isothermal oxidation at 900–1200 °C for up to 500 h
